flags.observation: Onboarding is one joke beat; nothing says who is speaking or what the listener is doing here, despite ample character budget.
No expert dog whistle from wrestling lore or history in the intro; only the name "Shahryār" rewards insiders.
"Under Shahryār's deadline: Shahryār, the Destroyer" says the name twice in one breath; opener on the first card bridges nothing.
"Dunyazad buys her sister time for: The Grand Vizier" builds a causal link the cards do not support; logic is muddled.
"The stolen commission buys" contradicts card 10, where the Sorcerer got "screwed out of the commission"; nothing stolen, nothing bought.
Object-acting in the opener: an abstraction performs a purchase in "The stolen commission buys".
"cosmic heat, three wishes, No DQ" recites almost the whole power text as a list, not as an aside.
Cutting "She doesn't want the Vizier's son" to "not the Vizier's son" makes the princess sound like she is not the son.
"ring collapse, a dried ring" is a power-name tail plus a fragment; meaning is lost, reads as padding.
"floor literally knives, razor terrain" drops the verb and appends the power name; fragment, not a sentence.
"The sailor hunts an exit from" repeats the opener family of beat 12 "The sailor loses his shore to" only three lines apart.
"monster heel": monster is absent from card 17 lore and power; "the squash match destroys them" has no referent.
"The wreck leads to another bargain": a thing as agent; no earlier bargain exists for "another" to refer to.
"hardcore valet, daggers" tacks power name onto the line; same label-tail pattern in beats 7, 16, 19, 24, 25.
"the botch, password" keeps the game reference from "play a 'Password' card" as a bare label without image.
Object-acting in the opener: a place behaves like a person in "The cave attracts a claimant".
"The thieves mark the door before:" ends on a dangling preposition; same noun-verb-preposition-colon template in beats 6, 9, 12, 15.
Openers mostly follow props (commission, wreck, cave, jar, door) rather than people; KayfabeTip 3 largely unmet.
"Behind the jar waits" links unrelated tales by location only; an and-then bridge, neither therefore nor but.
"tank class" is a gaming class term kept as a label in the line.
